name: Cached live-database reader
description: Serves structured queries over a consumer-supplied fetch function through a short-lived in-memory cache keyed on collection and canonical filter. It is thread-safe so the planner's parallel reads do not hammer the store, and nothing is synced to disk.
advantages: Reads live data where it lives, with cheap repeated reads inside the window and no sync job to keep fresh.
disadvantages: Data can be stale for the length of the cache window. It maps read and grep onto queries only where that makes sense, otherwise returning an unsupported observation.

name: Quest API context reader
description: Queries the Quest backend for goal metadata, notes, related goals, task history, decisions and reflections, and skips Quest queries when a task is local-only. It is designed to sit inside the composite beside file and database adapters.
advantages: Gives the planner the product's own structured context, including cross-environment discovery, in one source.
disadvantages: It is keyed by goal and quest identifiers rather than by a free-text question, so it cannot be ranked on question-driven retrieval and is pinned by decision tests instead. Keyed by goal and quest ids against the Quest API, not by a question, so it cannot be driven offline.

name: Source interface with shared channel flags
description: Defines the source contract (a name and a collect call that must never raise) and a base class whose class-level flags decide how the engine treats each channel: relevance judgment, admission judgment, ask tracking and relaying. The live engine and concrete channels build on it, so the rules are declared per channel rather than hard-coded in the engine.
advantages: New channels slot in by declaring flags, with no engine change. The card-scoped versus user-scoped split is stated once, with the incident that motivated it. Selected because: fixed in code
disadvantages: The flags are trust-based: a channel author who sets one wrong silently changes what is tracked or judged. It defines the contract only, so it cannot show on its own that the offered set is correct.

name: Live engine over fake quest channels
description: Runs the real update engine with the real notes, goal-update and decision sources against a fake client, selecting which channels are watched per case and applying the engine's own first-look window and open-ask bounds. It reports the sorted offered ids and the ids needing a response, with no model calls.
advantages: Exercises the shipped code path end to end, deterministically and free, so any change to the rules shows up as an exact-set mismatch.
disadvantages: The cases restate rules the code already follows, so passing is a regression pin rather than proof the rules are right. External channels such as mail, documents and chat are not covered because they need real accounts.

name: The update engine over its built-in channels
description: Gathers what changed on a card since it was last looked at from the channels the card watches (quest notes, goal updates, decisions, reflections, insights, Drive, mail, Notion, Google Chat) into one bundle, with no Quest client until a caller builds one.
advantages: One engine for every channel; a new channel is one more source, and one failing source never costs the others.
disadvantages: Without an account the channels that need one read nothing.

name: Registry of built-in and host resolvers
description: A small protocol plus a registry mapping item type to resolver, with built-in note and file resolvers, coercion of plain callables into resolvers, and host entries overriding built-ins. Missing types render an unresolved-pointer line and errors return empty text.
advantages: Generic, with no host specifics, and a bad pointer cannot break assembly. Hosts add types without changing the library. Selected because: fixed in code
disadvantages: A silent empty result can hide a broken host resolver unless the unresolved line is noticed, and freshness depends entirely on the host's data layer.

name: Production registry under scripted host resolvers
description: Drives the real registry builder and the real card-content renderer with scripted host resolvers (objects, callables, raising, empty) and file text, checking unresolved lines for every type, budgets, item caps and abridged summaries.
advantages: Free, deterministic coverage of the shipped path including failure containment.
disadvantages: Host data layers are fakes, so real latency and error shapes are not tested.

name: Parallel multi-source composite
description: Runs a list of member adapters in separate threads and merges the results: reads grouped by source and path, searches deduplicated, queries combined with source attribution, and discovery merged. For named reads it tries each member and keeps the first non-error answer.
advantages: A single adapter slot reaches every source, and one slow or failing member does not stop the others. Source attribution lets the planner cite where evidence came from. Selected because: RunnerConfig.retrieval (config_source_builders)
disadvantages: Unscoped searches are broadcast to every member, which costs more when a member is remote or paid. Merge rules are simple, so ranking across sources is not relevance-aware.

name: MCP server reader
description: Maps the discovery and read surface onto one MCP server: resources list and read for sources and sections, tools list and describe for operations, and tool calls for queries gated by an explicit allowlist. Every name is prefixed with an alias so servers never collide.
advantages: Reaches any MCP-speaking system without bespoke code, and the allowlist keeps a tool it was not granted from ever being called.
disadvantages: Search is delegated to the server so its quality varies, and plain regex search is not supported. It is read-only by design, so mutations need the separate write adapter.

name: Notion database reader
description: A read-only adapter over a configured set of Notion databases: list them, query rows with simple filters, read a page's properties and bounded block text, and search across rows. Auth is injected, only configured databases may be read, and only reads can be sent.
advantages: Two locks make it incapable of writing, and it grounds answers in structured team records the other sources do not hold.
disadvantages: Locates rows by title and properties rather than body text, so content inside a page is hard to find. It depends on a pinned API version and the integration's access.

name: Drive document reader
description: Lists folders and reads file text from a workspace drive (documents, sheets, PDFs, plain text) through the standard retrieval surface, with injected auth and lazy PDF support. Unsupported types and permission errors return error observations.
advantages: Brings shared documents into the planner's reach without copying them, and failures never break the loop.
disadvantages: Drive offers no search here, so the policy is to list and read, which scales poorly on large folders. PDF text depends on an optional package.

name: Chat conversation reader
description: Lists spaces, pulls recent messages and groups them into conversations by thread or space, exposing them through read, search and query, with optional pre-flight assembly. Auth is injected and failures come back as error observations.
advantages: Lets answers draw on discussion that never reached a document, and supports incremental fetch of messages since a point in time.
disadvantages: Chat is noisy, so relevance depends on good scoping, and it needs a delegated-access service identity. Reading is bounded by what the credential may see.

name: Local file tree reader
description: Reads and greps files under one configured root using only regular expressions and directory walking, with no shell. It resolves paths through the shared containment check, skips secret-like, binary and oversize files, and returns partial hits within a wall-clock grep budget.
advantages: Fast, dependency-free and strictly read-only, with a hard boundary that the write side shares, so there is one implementation of containment.
disadvantages: Keyword and regex only, so a paraphrase misses. Huge trees return partial hits when the time budget runs out.

name: Remote file server reader
description: Reads files on another machine through a file-serving endpoint using the planner's ordinary file vocabulary, namespaced by alias. It refuses names without its alias before any network call, does not follow redirects, caps response size and never leaks the access token in errors.
advantages: Extends the same read vocabulary to other machines with safe failure and no credential leakage, and search results can be pasted straight into a read.
disadvantages: Every search costs a network round trip and so must be scoped. It depends on the remote server being reachable and, like the local reader, matches by pattern rather than meaning.

name: Offline lifecycle harness
description: Runs the real poller, executor, persona resolver, folder sync, scheduling helper and lane helpers against a fake client and a scripted model, with no model calls.
advantages: Deterministic and free coverage of the whole lifecycle including duplicates, lost claims and team scoping. Selected because: runner/config_wiring.py (a lane's run_lane drives Poller and TaskExecutor)
disadvantages: The fake client hides wire-level behaviour such as HTTP errors and real payload shapes, and crash recovery of orphaned claims is not yet covered.

name: Task poller and claimer
description: Discovers due tasks per scan, deduplicates by signature across restarts, claims through the backend, hands each task to the executor with bounded concurrency, and pauses pickup when the host is overloaded.
advantages: Event-driven, restart-safe, and degrades instead of crashing on transient errors.
disadvantages: Large and stateful, with several guards that interact, so edge cases such as orphaned claims are hard to see.

name: Single-task executor
description: Runs one claimed task through the orchestrator and maps the result onto a status report: answer or met deep run is done, a short deep run is incomplete or failed, a decision is needs-you, a cancelled task gets no report. It never raises to the poller.
advantages: One clear unit of work that is easy to test with a mock client and stub brain.
disadvantages: The mapping from result to status is policy that must stay in step with the backend's status vocabulary.

name: Shared lane entry point
description: Provides the check, once and loop-forever driver with argument parsing, env-file loading, local-time due gating and degrade-instead-of-crash behaviour on incomplete config.
advantages: Removes the duplicated glue each consumer used to write.
disadvantages: Consumers must fit its argv shape, and the local-time gate patches behaviour globally.

name: Configured persona resolver
description: Chooses who runs a task from configuration, in order: a structured assignment field matching the registry, an optional model-judged explicit ask, then domain dominance, with optional auto-registration of unknown ids.
advantages: Replaces hand-written resolvers, needs no model call for structural lanes, and never activates on a bare name mention.
disadvantages: The judged and dominance steps depend on model judgement, and a wrong registry entry misroutes work.

name: In-memory thread-safe inbox
description: Holds a dictionary of per-conversation lists behind a lock inside the library's inbox module, satisfying the port with push, drain and peek. The orchestrator drains it between planner steps. Measured by plugging it into the live orchestrator and running synthetic cases where messages are pushed before or during a run, plus direct port-contract operations, with no model calls.
advantages: Simple, fast, thread-safe, and app-agnostic, so the same inbox serves chat, a frontend or anything else; the measurement checks delivery through the real planning loop and catches loss or cross-conversation leaks. Selected because: fixed in code
disadvantages: State is lost on restart and is not shared across processes or hosts, so a multi-process deployment needs a different implementation; the cases do not cover the deep retry boundary where a subprocess cannot be re-prompted.

name: One vision-model call per image (today)
description: Each attached image is sent to the configured vision model with a describe prompt and the text is added to the grounding.
advantages: Built; the only arm that makes the model call.
disadvantages: Not measured; its cost, time and value are unknown until the metric is built.

name: No description, the image is named only (proposed)
description: Proposed. The image is listed by name and type with no description, so no vision call is made.
advantages: No cost; no image data leaves the process.
disadvantages: The reply cannot use what is in the image; not built.

name: Channels, terminal and package as ways in
description: Each way in is its own measured solution, and every one hands its request to the same router. The package's front door is taught by its documents (explain-qar), shown by its examples (learn-by-example) and set up through one layered configuration (configure-a-lane).
advantages: A new channel is one more solution beneath this one, measured on its own.
disadvantages: No metric judges the ways in together; only each one's own.

name: Work-folder sync
description: Mirrors a work item's state and notes into a local file with runner-managed marked sections, and pushes new human notes back once, preserving human-authored text elsewhere in the file.
advantages: Idempotent, keeps human edits, and uses only the existing client methods.
disadvantages: A single shared file can conflict with hand edits near the markers, and direction rules must be respected by callers.

name: Quest HTTP client from the environment
description: Builds the Quest client from QUEST_BASE_URL (or QUEST_API_URL), QUEST_API_KEY and, when set, QUEST_TEAM_ID, so the runner works in the account those name.
advantages: One client for every consumer of the runner; nothing to pass when the environment is set.
disadvantages: Reads one account; a deployment that serves several teams passes its own client.

name: Read back what a change touched (proposed)
description: Proposed. After every operation the objects it touched are re-read and placed in the working stream, replacing older views of them for the rest of the session.
advantages: The AI's own changes never contradict what it says next; one small read per change.
disadvantages: Changes made by others still lag until the next read; not built.

name: A live read behind every state claim (proposed)
description: Proposed. Every claim about account state needs a live read in the same turn; no card is used for state.
advantages: Always current, including others' changes.
disadvantages: A read on every state question costs time on the reply path; not built.

name: Managed quest card plus optional live reads (today)
description: A managed card per quest, rebuilt when the quest syncs, grounds each turn, and the planner issues live reads through the host's retrieval adapter when it wants more.
advantages: Built; cheap; one card per quest that every surface shares.
disadvantages: The card lags changes made since the last sync, including the AI's own; reads are optional; nothing is read back after a change, so two answers in a session can rest on different reads.

name: Direct tool-call ablation
description: One model call is given the quest record and the tool schemas and returns the tool calls as JSON, which the registry then executes. There is no planner and no answer step, so it is the upper bound on what the direct path alone can do for a plain edit.
advantages: The cheapest model path: a single call, no scaffolding. It shows how far plain edits can go without a planner.
disadvantages: It cannot read, answer, confirm or start a deep run, and it struggles with multi-step or ambiguous requests. It trusts one unchecked call to write, so it is not a replacement for the brain. Cheaper but cannot carry out multi-step or ambiguous requests.

name: Fake-client allowlist check
description: Runs the production writer against a fake client at the process edge to check listing, exact tool and arguments once, aliased and bare names, refusals with zero calls, server error and dead connection.
advantages: Offline, fast and precise about what reached the client.
disadvantages: A fake client cannot show how real servers behave, so protocol quirks are untested.

name: Planner-only orchestration
description: The whole brain handles the turn: the planner decides, the tool runs through the registry and a reply is composed, with the deep runner disabled so deep requests come back unexecuted. A fresh orchestrator and scratch corpus are built per case so no case sees another's turns.
advantages: Every message gets the full planning treatment, including reads, confirms and clarifies, so it is the most capable path and the reference for quality.
disadvantages: Pays for a planning call even on a plain create. Simple requests take more turns and tokens than they need.

name: MCP operation writer
description: Lists the allow-listed subset of a server's tools as writable operations and executes one by name through the client, refusing anything off the allowlist before the network, with alias namespacing and an audit detail on every result.
advantages: Strong guard and full auditability for each attempt, sharing a connection with the read adapter while keeping a separate policy. Selected because: config_resolvers.resolve_mcp_write_runners
disadvantages: Allowlist hygiene is on the host, and a call is not idempotent, so a retry after an ambiguous failure could repeat a mutation.

name: Maintained view per quest only (proposed)
description: Proposed. After each request a cheap model rewrites, in the background, a short note for the quest of what was decided, declined, learned and is next, each line citing its source; every request on that quest reads it first. This is the lowest level of the hierarchy, with nothing above it.
advantages: Simple; the fence stays the existing per-quest tag; no time added before the reply.
disadvantages: Nothing learned at an intent above the quest reaches it, which is the gap the owner named; a wrong line persists until corrected; not built.

name: Periodic reflection on the best tier (proposed)
description: Proposed. On a schedule a best-tier model reviews a quest's recent requests and outcomes and writes its long view.
advantages: A true long view from few calls.
disadvantages: Stale between runs; best-tier cost; not built.

name: One view per intent, cascading down (proposed)
description: Proposed. One maintained view per intent, shared by any representative serving it; a request reads the view of its quest's intent and of each ancestor, nearest first, within a budget, fenced so a view reaches only its intent's descendants.
advantages: Follows the host's hierarchy directly; one view per intent whoever serves it; reuses the placements and parent links the host already stores.
disadvantages: Representatives with different roles share one view and blur it; deep chains cost tokens; needs a fence that knows ancestors; not built.

name: One view per representative across its assigned quests, placed in the hierarchy (proposed, recommended)
description: Proposed. Each AI representative keeps one maintained high-level view across the quests assigned to it (decisions, declines, corrections, learned notes, where the work is heading), anchored at the lowest intent that holds those quests and reading that intent's ancestors within a budget. A request it handles reads that view and the parts of its single quest's detail that bear on it. Its existing learned notes and context preferences are filed under the quest or intent they were learned in, so they gain the same fence.
advantages: Matches the owner's model: the representative and its assigned quests are the unit, with a broad view across them; reuses the host's quest assignments, roles and intent placements; gives the representative's notes the scope they lack today.
disadvantages: A representative's quests may sit under several intents, so the anchor can be wide; the view must be rebuilt when an assignment changes; notes learned before this have no quest or intent and must be placed or kept global; needs the fence that knows assignments and ancestors; not built.

name: Separate stores read at the start of a request (today)
description: Conversation recall, recent context, feedback guidance, predictions, reflections and quest cards are each read separately at the start of a request and prepended to the context block, fenced per quest or global; a representative's learned notes and context preferences are read with no scope; declined proposals arrive from the host's escalation history.
advantages: Built; each store is measured on its own; a failure in one does not stop the others.
disadvantages: No view of what an intent or the quest settled; several budgets and paths, each of which must apply the fence; the representative's notes cross quests; chat and background work read different subsets.

name: Shared quest ranker
description: Which quest a piece of text belongs to, for every surface that picks one: daily plan goals, reflection notes, insights' quests field, the AI task form, chat task pickup and task delegation. The quests' own embeddings lead the candidates, the model only picks which numbered quests a text is about (or none), and the user's priority orders them. quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_selection.py (rank_quest_batch, select_and_rank_quests_for_text).
advantages: One shared path, so a better pick improves every surface at once; a wrong quest is answered with none, not a guess; a few output tokens per text.
disadvantages: No labelled case set or recorded accuracy yet, only unit tests (tests/api/endpoints/daily_plan/test_rank_goal_quests.py, tests/test_reflection_notes_ranker_failure.py). Its past alternatives were replaced without a measured comparison: the model ordering the quests (before e1736906), each surface prompting its own pick such as the daily plan prompt (before 9b1c791b), and the first-priority quest as the fallback (before 7fb9cfec).

name: Rank quests by words and meaning, with evidence
description: Ranks a person's own quests for a chat message by IDF-weighted word overlap plus embedding similarity, with the model judging which terms actually identify a quest, and returns evidence snippets saying where each match came from. Used by Quest AI chat to resolve which quest a message names. quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_candidates.py (rank_quests_for_message, lexical_rank, semantic_quest_candidates).
advantages: Shows its evidence, so the caller can show its work instead of asserting a match; the lexical signal catches named quests that embeddings blur.
disadvantages: A second classifier doing much of the same job as shared-quest-ranker, on a different code path; never compared with it on the same cases (tests/test_quest_candidates.py are unit tests).

name: Per-consumer worker
description: Each product writes its own worker and chat backend around a model vendor's API.
advantages: Fits its one product exactly; no shared-library coordination.
disadvantages: The plumbing is rebuilt and drifts per product (the history that led to QAR); improvements do not travel; chat and tasks diverge.

name: Agent framework with Quest glue
description: Build the engine from a general framework (LangGraph, CrewAI, an agent SDK) and add Quest grounding, escalation and the executor as glue.
advantages: Mature building blocks, community and tooling; less code of our own for the loop.
disadvantages: Grounding, scope containment, escalation, the executor and measured selection still have to be built; framework churn becomes a dependency risk.

name: Deep runner only
description: Hand every task straight to a coding agent such as Claude Code with the person's material available, with no routing or answering loop in front.
advantages: Strong at real multi-step work; very little engine code.
disadvantages: Slow and costly for simple questions; weaker grounding in Quest's own state; escalation and scope still need building; one vendor dependency.

name: Live chat on a disposable world
description: Drives the real in-app chat end to end on a disposable development account, running each case in a fresh conversation and restoring the world afterwards. Hard deterministic pre-checks run first, then a model judge scores the transcript against the case rubric and named pivot facts. It counts model calls and tokens when run in process.
advantages: Measures the true behaviour of the shipped brain on realistic data, including routing and side effects, and records the judge's reasons per case so failures can be read. Selected because: the Quest AI chat in the app, which runs this checkout's brain (core/orchestrator.py); the dev arm drives it end to end
disadvantages: Expensive, since a case is many model calls, and slow. It needs a development backend and a built world, the judge is not calibrated against human verdicts, and a small sample is noisy enough that one case can pass and then fail.

name: Offline metric validity check
description: No Quest and no model: for each case it validates the case against the dataset schema, checks that the deterministic pre-checks accept a reference reply built from the case's own expected phrases, and checks that they reject an empty reply. It proves the scoring is able to tell a good reply from none.
advantages: Free and deterministic, catches broken or vacuous cases before any spend, and keeps the offline suite green when no development account exists.
disadvantages: It says nothing about how well the chat actually answers. Its reference reply is derived from the case itself, so it cannot reveal a rubric that is wrong or too easy.

name: QAR as shipped, live on the subscription (today)
description: The orchestrator built the way production builds it, with the claude CLI backend on the cheapest tier, the real tool catalogue and the real send command, over the placeholder account.
advantages: Built; measures the true path including the model's decisions; costs subscription time, not API dollars.
disadvantages: Varies between runs; a small set; the placeholder account is not a real Quest.

name: Scripted ideal planner (offline)
description: The same orchestrator and tool catalogue with a planner that replays each case's ideal decisions and reply.
advantages: Free and deterministic; proves the cases and the scorer separate right from wrong and that the code around the model does not spoil a right decision.
disadvantages: Says nothing about how a model decides.

name: Rules only, no model (floor)
description: No orchestrator: a few message shapes become a note, a goal or a queued task, everything else gets a fixed non-answer, and the terminal prints the fixed Queued line.
advantages: No cost, instant; shows what the set rewards without a model.
disadvantages: Fails every question about the account and every web question.

name: One turn of the orchestrator over the model
description: The loop plans, gathers, re-plans and answers one message over the model seat, with no cards behind it, and returns the reply, how the loop ended and what ran.
advantages: The shipped loop as one call, built the way the whole runner builds it.
disadvantages: Holds no cards or Quest account; a caller who needs them uses the whole runner.

name: The shipped path as one call
description: Answers a message with one turn of the loop over the model and returns the turn whole, which is the path the end-to-end metric measures.
advantages: No second wiring of the loop: the measured path is the one that runs.
disadvantages: Holds no cards or Quest account; the whole runner is the arm that has them.

name: quest-ai-runner library
description: A domain-free Python library: a bounded plan, gather, re-plan, answer loop that escalates to a deep runner when real work is needed (the core), a task executor that polls Quest, claims, runs, escalates and reports (the runner), and reference adapters for retrieval, model providers, cards, vectors, web research and deep runners, all wired by one configuration per lane and each swappable part chosen by metric.
advantages: One engine for chat and scheduled work; grounded in the consumer's sources; escalation built in; open source and reusable outside Quest; every part measured and swappable.
disadvantages: A large codebase to maintain; chat answer quality is currently weak on the cheapest model; some parts are measured only offline; consumers must keep adapters in step with the library.

name: Eligibility gate mixin
description: Methods on the autopilot pass that test, in order, daily budget, cadence in the quest's zone, Run now, reactive trigger, roster day and backpressure, and read open asks, so a quest is skipped with a reason before any goal is read.
advantages: Cheap, ordered and explainable gates that follow the person's settings exactly.
disadvantages: The ordering and interplay of many rules is intricate, and a new setting needs a matching case.

name: Scripted-client gate evaluation arm
description: Runs the production autopilot pass for one quest against a client that answers only what a gate reads and a pinned clock, recording anything reached past the gates, so the outcome is exactly a skip reason or passage.
advantages: Tests the real gates deterministically with no model calls. Selected because: think_critically/autopilot_gates.py GatesMixin._gate_quest, the budget check in AutopilotPass.run and the pure predicates in runner/autopilot_periods.py
disadvantages: Measures only the decision to run, not the work after it.

name: Stream, milestone and fan-out sinks
description: The stream sink forwards every event to the consumer's stream, the milestone sink forwards only the always-surfacing event types to named callbacks, and the fan-out sink sends live events to both and supports detaching the live side. A failing forward or callback never breaks the run.
advantages: Policy lives in one place so every consumer inherits it, and failures in a consumer cannot stop the work. Selected because: Mode selects StreamSink or MilestoneSink
disadvantages: Policy is fixed by event type, so a consumer wanting a different split must write a sink, and swallowed failures can hide a dead stream.

name: Sink policy cases
description: Builds the production sinks and feeds them event sequences for live, background, handoff and broken-stream cases, recording what each surfaced.
advantages: Offline and deterministic, and exercises the real sinks, including the failure paths.
disadvantages: Scores the sinks only; it cannot say whether the orchestrator emits the right events.

name: Milestone sink
description: A background sink that surfaces only result, decision, milestone, context and done events to named callbacks.
advantages: A quiet default for background work: the person sees outcomes and decisions only.
disadvantages: A consumer wanting a different split must write a sink.

name: Fixed status line, no model call (floor, proposed)
description: Proposed. The first beat is a fixed line chosen from the turn's mode and first event, with no model call.
advantages: No cost and no delay.
disadvantages: Says less about this turn; not built.

name: One model call writes the explanation from the trace (today)
description: After a turn that answered, a structured call writes the explanation from the trace at the configured explanation tier.
advantages: Built; the only arm that makes the model call.
disadvantages: Not measured; its cost, time and value are unknown until the metric is built.

name: Template over the trace, no model call (floor, proposed)
description: Proposed. The explanation is assembled from the trace entries by a fixed template, with no model call.
advantages: No cost, no delay, cannot invent a step.
disadvantages: Reads as a log, not as prose; not built.

name: Nothing shown (the status quo before the Trail)
description: The app shows no trace of the work: dots, then the answer.
advantages: Nothing to get wrong, nothing added to the screen. Selected because: not selected; it is the incumbent the others are measured against.
disadvantages: The person cannot see that the answer rests on real work, so a turn with work shows nothing.

name: A plain list of every step
description: One row per step in arrival order with every item listed under it, live and settled, whether or not the answer used it.
advantages: Complete, and nothing is hidden behind a tap.
disadvantages: Shows counts of internal work and items the answer did not use; a long run grows the page.

name: Behaviour before the build (no interim for an unmet attempt)
description: The unmet attempt sends no interim message (the earlier interim needed done evidence and analysis); the person gets the final answer only.
advantages: Nothing to get wrong. Selected because: not selected; the incumbent the others are measured against (a reconstruction).
disadvantages: The person cannot tell whether work continues.

name: An interim on every unmet attempt (spam baseline)
description: Every attempt that did not meet the goal sends an interim.
advantages: Never silent. Selected because: not selected; a baseline.
disadvantages: Repeats itself, sends before blockers that are not more work and ignores spacing and the cap.

name: The terminal draws the Trail from the hub's renderers
description: The chat terminal shows a live row of the newest page opened, a one-line summary of what was read that opens in place, interim updates folded into one row, an ask as a block answered by number or words, and a stopped reason with Continue. The rules and sentences are the hub's terminal renderers (the same words as the Quest app); QAR only draws their blocks, binds keys and sends the answer through the Quest client.
advantages: No second copy of the rules or the words in QAR; the Quest app's wording is checked against the hub's by a drift test. Selected because: not selected; it is the only terminal arm.
disadvantages: Drawn and tested headless only; never used by a person in a real terminal, and not measured on real turns. The interim updates need QAR_INTERIM_REPLIES=1. The terminal's turn still runs through QAR's own orchestrator, not a hub run function (none exists yet).

name: One cheap model call per turn writes the beat (today)
description: The narrator asks the turn's model for one short line from the events so far; a refusal or error is dropped and never fails the turn.
advantages: Built; the only arm that makes the model call.
disadvantages: Not measured; its cost, time and value are unknown until the metric is built.

name: The Trail (live line, one summary line, expandable groups)
description: A live line (the newest active kind) while working, one summary line after (records first, then sites, then papers, at most three clauses), and groups behind a tap with five rows each; the same reduced form for every viewer of a shared thread.
advantages: One line by default and nothing for a turn without work. Selected because: it is the arm built and mounted on all three chat surfaces (the incumbent), not because it passed the most real turns. Best guess, not significant. Measured by metric-work-trace-experience (rows in the results log): offline on hand-written turns that were edited after failures and have no held-out set, the Trail clears every rule and the plain list fails the idle-turn and failed-search turns; on the cheap real tier (web, own records, papers, unrelated) and on the ten-turn real tier (web, Rust, Go, own records, logged runs, quest ranking, two papers questions, a group thread, an unrelated question) after the 2026-11-01 wording fixes (live line names the newest opened page, the summary names what was used, removed links said in plain words) and a judge that now reads the whole reply, the Trail passed more turns than the plain list and than showing nothing, and more of its shown elements were judged to earn their place, and the truthfulness gate failed on no real turn. The Trail is the highest scorer and the incumbent, so it stays selected; 7 against 3 on ten turns was not repeated, so it is a best guess, not significant, and not held-out because the elements were edited on the failures of these same turns. Judge: the `claude-sonnet` family alias on the Claude Code subscription (the CLI picks the newest sonnet, the exact id is not logged), one call per turn, arm and run, rubric JUDGE_RULE in evaluation/components/work_trace_experience/score.py, strict and noisy (it once called a correct count of five cited papers a conflict: a harness fault, it was shown only the first 900 characters of the reply, now the whole). The turns were captured on Haiku `claude-haiku-5-5` with a seeded fictional card store whose titles are realistic; the emitter was fixed on failures seen in these same turns, so they are not held out.
disadvantages: Three elements still fail on the ten turns: a bare count of a shared thread's records (the privacy rule forbids naming them), the removed-link sentence on a turn whose reply holds no link (the judge cannot see what was removed), and a named record the emitter wrongly counted as used (a false positive of the word-overlap rule in core/work_trace.py). The words are composed in quest-frontend workTrace.ts and the judge sees the same strings. A record counts only when the planner took it and the reply draws on it (title, three consecutive words, or two shared long words), so a record the reply restates in other words or the planner did not note is not counted (an undercount, never an overcount), and the records step is sent once when the reply is final, so there is no live records line. A card with no short name of its own (a vector hit gives only a slice of its text) is not counted. Real turns use a seeded fictional card store, not real Quest data; Haiku sometimes answers a current-facts question without searching, so web turns are not guaranteed to exercise the web step.

name: The structural gate of core/interim_policy.py
description: Sends only when the verdict is more work, the loop runs again, no ask is open, there is a reason and something to show, something new since the last message, and the cap and spacing allow. The same arm files the one ask a person-only block needs (core/ask_policy.py): it asks when the verdict needs a person with a question, or a tool fails on an access refusal, resolves the teammate or falls back to the asker, and keeps one key per turn and gap.
advantages: Every condition is structural. Selected because: it is the policy in code and passes the offline cases; the switch is off by default.
disadvantages: Not measured on real turns yet.

name: Decision-request sink
description: Adapts the Quest client into the escalation port: it resolves an assignee (explicit, then default, then the quest owner), refuses to file an unaddressed ask, applies a deadline default, and creates a hold-default team decision request whose identifier it returns.
advantages: Never files an ask nobody will see, and puts decisions where the team already works. Selected because: RunnerConfig.escalation (defaults to QuestDecisionSink)
disadvantages: Tied to one backend's decision model, and a missing owner or backend failure surfaces as an error rather than a quiet fallback.

name: Fake-backend delivery check
description: Runs the production sink against an in-memory fake client, checking the assignee fallback chain, kind, default, deadline, review link, team routing, repeated asks and backend failure.
advantages: Offline and exact about what was filed and to whom.
disadvantages: Scores delivery and detail only, not whether the brain chose to escalate, and the fake cannot show real backend behaviour.

name: Creator keeps the goal, no model call (floor, proposed)
description: Proposed. A new goal stays with its creator unless the person assigns it.
advantages: No cost, no surprise assignment.
disadvantages: Goals an AI could have taken wait for a person; not built.

name: Two small model verdicts when a goal is created (today)
description: On a shared quest, a small model names the likely assignee and judges doability for an AI representative.
advantages: Built; the only arm that makes the model call.
disadvantages: Not measured; its cost, time and value are unknown until the metric is built.

name: Persona resolver precedence for queued tasks (today)
description: A structured assignment field first, then a model-judged explicit ask, then domain-card dominance with names excluded, then a structural fallback; a bare mention never selects.
advantages: Built; no model call when the task names its owner; never raises, falling back to the plain assistant.
disadvantages: Used for queued tasks only; does not know the thread a task came from; its accuracy on a labelled set is not measured.

name: Host chat classifier among assigned representatives (today, in the host)
description: The host's chat picks among the quest's assigned representatives the person can see with one fast-model call, falling back to the person's default representative.
advantages: Built; cheap; respects per-viewer visibility; only assigned representatives are candidates.
disadvantages: Lives in the host, not the library; unmeasured; the tasks a chat spawns may run as someone else.

name: A thread keeps its representative (proposed)
description: Proposed. Once a thread has a representative, every task and pass it spawns runs as that representative unless the person names another, and the choice is recorded on the task.
advantages: Removes the one-thread, many-voices failure seen in production; no model call.
disadvantages: A task that truly needs another representative's role must be named explicitly; not built.

name: Fit by role, assigned quests and intent branch (proposed)
description: Proposed. Among a quest's assigned representatives, the one whose role text and assigned quests (and the intent branch they sit in) best cover the request is chosen, scored without a model where clear and with one small call on the borderline.
advantages: Uses what the host already stores; ties the choice to whose higher mind fits the request.
disadvantages: Free-text roles are uneven; borderline cases cost a call; not built.

name: Ask the person on an equal fit (proposed)
description: Proposed. When two representatives fit equally, the person is asked once which should handle it, and the answer is remembered for that kind of request on that quest.
advantages: Never guesses on a real tie; the answer becomes a label.
disadvantages: Each question costs the person attention; must stay rare; not built.
